answer: Honeypots with known-bad answers are cheap to run and catch copiers immediately. Any attempt to link two identities resets both to zero, so a spiral of mutual vouching costs more than it returns. Auditors rotate, which removes the option of buying the same grader twice. A beacon of new accounts shining on a honeypot is just a list of who to ignore. The wander ends when probing costs more than one honest receipt pays.
